sources.citation: Cahill, Peter T. 2012. Usted es haragán pero vos sos lazy: Initialization in Honduran Sign Language. BPhil thesis, University of Pittsburgh (Linguistics / University Honors College). 91 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic study of initialization (fingerspelled-letter handshapes) and Deaf-community ideology; sec. 3.4 'Introduction to LESHO' (pp. 27-31) covers only classification and socio-history. p. 27: 'Williams (2010), the only linguist to have published on Honduran Sign Language, states that it has many similarities to ASL, but also to Mexican and Costa Rican Sign Languages'. No stress/prosody/accent/intonation hits in the full text.

sources.citation: Parks, Jason. 2011. Sign language word list comparisons: Toward a replicable coding and scoring methodology. MA thesis, University of North Dakota. 98 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 2.1.2 'Phonological basis of coding system' (pp. 9-11) only defines handshape/location/movement parameters for Levenshtein wordlist comparison across 4 Honduran varieties (Tegucigalpa, Juticalpa, San Pedro Sula, El Progreso) and other Latin American sign languages; only 'stress' string is 'accentuated' (p. 5 context) and the Brentari 1998 'prosodic model' reference.
